Round 2174.decision_summary:
Open-debt item 551: a selector carrying ONE non-ASCII byte outside quotes
killed the process, and the four published doors that reach the lexer all
carried it. Filed from a CONSUMER's measurement -- the zenoh-analyzer
session read it in its own repository, changed nothing here, and
reported. This round closes it.

THE MECHANISM, RE-MEASURED RATHER THAN QUOTED. `lex` walked
`source.as_bytes()` and turned each byte into a `char` with `as`. That is
not a UTF-8 decode; it is a LATIN-1 REINTERPRETATION. A UTF-8 lead byte
`0xC2..=0xF4` becomes `'Â'..'ô'`, and `char::is_alphanumeric` accepts most
of them, so `is_word_char` let the word scan step INTO a multi-byte
character. The continuation bytes `0x80..=0xBF` mostly are not word
characters, so the scan stopped one byte in, and `&source[i..j]` sliced
off a char boundary and panicked.

⚠ AND THE SECOND ROUTE, which the consumer named in a correction and this
round's derived corpus found independently: `©` and `€` are NOT
alphanumeric, yet they died too. Their lead bytes (`0xC2`, `0xE2`) read
as accented Latin letters, which ARE. So the word scan started on a
character that is not a word character at all. A fix that only taught
`is_word_char` to reject high bytes would have passed every Korean case
in the report and still mis-lexed these. THE CAST IS THE DEFECT, not the
predicate.

WHAT THE FIX IS NOT. It is not a switch to character counting.
`wz_dissect.h` publishes `at` as a BYTE offset and a consumer places a
caret from it, so `i` stays a byte index and is advanced by `len_utf8()`.
A fix that made slicing safe by counting characters would have moved
every caret in every selector containing a multi-byte character -- a
silent regression in the exact consumer that reported this.

THE LANGUAGE DECISION THIS FORCED, and it was not in the item. Once the
walk yields real characters, `is_word_char` reaches its Unicode arm for
the first time -- and that arm calls `char::is_alphanumeric`, not
`is_ascii_alphanumeric`. Admitting non-ASCII letters unquoted is what
this lexer was WRITTEN to do; the byte cast made that arm unreachable
code that looked live. So `key == 로봇` is now ACCEPTED and parses to the
same filter as `key == "로봇"`, which is pinned by a test rather than
left to be discovered. `key == €` is REFUSED, naming `'€'` -- the
character the operator typed, where the old code would have cited `'â'`,
the mojibake of its lead byte.

THE INSTRUMENT IS A PROPERTY, NOT THE SEVEN REPORTED STRINGS, which is
the item's own instruction. Seven strings cannot separate "fixed" from
"fixed for these seven": what broke was that EVERY multi-byte character
was mis-lexed, and the ones that panicked were the ones whose lead byte
happened to be accepted. The corpus is DERIVED -- one character per UTF-8
length on both sides of `is_word_char`, crossed with twelve positions the
lexer takes different paths for -- and its own population is asserted, so
an emptied list is a failure rather than a pass.

Round 2180.decision_summary:
Open-debt item 554: the census document does not say WHICH of its
top-level keys are PLANES, so a consumer reading a `null` cannot tell an
absent plane from a key that never was one. Filed by R2179 from a
CONSUMING surface's request. This round closes it, and re-measuring the
item found the same defect in four more places than it was filed with.

THE ITEM'S OWN CLAIM, RE-MEASURED AND HOLDING. An emitted census carries
SEVEN top-level keys. With the network codecs, FIVE carry
`narrowed_by_selector` and none is null; without them, two carry the
marker and `exchanges` / `payloads` / `interests` arrive as `null`. So
the consumer's structural rule -- a top-level object holding that key is
a plane -- is exactly right for a plane this build can feed and says
nothing at all about one it cannot. What was left was the guess "a
top-level null is an absent plane": true of this library, promised by
nothing, and the consumer wrote that distinction down itself.

AND THE RE-MEASUREMENT FOUND THE COPY IS EVERYWHERE, WHICH IS THE ITEM'S
OWN ARGUMENT TURNED ON THE UPSTREAM. The item was filed with one stale
sentence -- the module doc saying "the two keys are emitted as null" over
three. MEASURED, five more: `census_json`'s title said "the four ANALYSIS
planes"; `census_json_where`'s doc said "Three of the four planes take a
selector" over five, of which TWO are unnarrowed and its own body says
so; `Dissection::message_lists`, the door whose whole paragraph is about
a list going stale, named four of the five planes that walk it and missed
`interest`; the C ABI's census door and `wz_dissect.h` each named four
planes to a linking consumer; and the fixture was CALLED
`four_plane_capture` while feeding five. A cardinal in an identifier is
the same copy as one in prose and is read by every author who writes a
test against it.

THE FIX IS IN THE DOCUMENT, NOT BESIDE IT. `DocumentShape` gains
`planes`: per revision, the top-level keys that are planes.
`envelope_into` writes it, so the census opens
`{"document":{"name":"census","revision":5,"planes":[...]}}` and the list
travels with the revision. The alternative considered was a second axis
on `wz_dissect_readable_surfaces` beside `value_families`, and it was
rejected on a property that was MEASURED rather than assumed: that door
describes the LIBRARY, while the census crosses the ABI as an owned
string a caller may store, forward or compare against an earlier one --
so a separately fetched plane list can be paired with a document from
another build with nothing able to notice.

⚠ AND ONE JUSTIFICATION THIS ROUND WROTE WAS REFUTED BY ITS OWN CHECK.
The first draft argued the envelope because "the command line writes a
census to a file". It does not: `wz-analyze --json` renders the CLI's own
report and `census_json` reaches a consumer only through
`wz-capi-dissect`. The claim was struck and replaced with the owned-string
argument above, which is a fact of this ABI. Prose nobody measures is what
this whole item is about; the round nearly shipped one.

WHY DOCUMENTS WITH NO PLANE STAY SILENT. Five of the six declare none,
and making them emit `planes:[]` would move five revisions to say
"nothing here" -- and this module's own argument is that the only safe
response to a moved number is to re-check, so that costs five audits that
buy nothing. Silence is safe because it is CHECKED, not observed: no
document may emit a top-level `null` it has not declared, so a document
with no `planes` key is one that has been shown it can never hand a
consumer an ambiguous one.

Round 2182.decision_summary:
Open-debt item 555, from the consuming surface: `fields[].kind` is a key a
consumer SWITCHES on and no revision declared its words. It cost that
surface a word outright -- it read seven and never had an `opaque` arm.

WHERE THE POPULATION CAME FROM, WHICH IS THE WHOLE OF THIS ROUND. The item
was filed with an explicit warning: source-counting had already been wrong
three times over this one key, in both directions, by both parties. So the
population was derived from an ARTIFACT first -- the every-plane fixture's
field document was emitted and its `kind` values read back. It reports
SEVEN words, and the missing one is `opaque`.

That measurement DECIDED the design rather than confirming it. A
vocabulary derived from the artifact alone would have shipped with exactly
the hole the consumer had, because no capture in this tree produces an
`Opaque` field. So the artifact is the cross-check and the POPULATION is a
walk over the type: `FieldValue::kind_word` / `kind_words`, promoted out of
`wz-session-core`'s own `mod tests` where it had been living. It had been
there all along -- a successor chain holding the eight words against a
rename and against each other, and against nothing a consumer could read.

`push_json` now CALLS `kind_word`, so the word on the wire and the word in
the vocabulary are one thing rather than two that agree today. What each
arm still owns is the companion key, which is a different fact.

THE JUDGEMENT ON `opaque`'s MISSING COMPANION KEY, which the item asked
for. It is NOT declared here, and that is a measurement rather than a
deferral. Rendering every arm gives eight words over THREE companion
shapes (`value`, `fields`, none). Rendering the field document's OTHER
discriminant family, `payload_decode.state`, gives eight words over SIX.
So "which keys accompany which value" is a THIRD axis of the document
contract beside the key set and the vocabulary, with a population of at
least two families in this one document. Declaring it for `opaque` alone
would be an exception, and putting a `carries` field on `ValueFamily` for
one cell of it would leave nine families holding an unchecked empty
default -- which is the hole R2181 had just finished closing on `planes`.

Round 2183.decision_summary:
R2182 closed open-debt item 555 by declaring the `fields[].kind` vocabulary
at field-document revision 3, with the words coming from
`FieldValue::kind_words` -- a walk over the type rather than a written list.
This round re-measured that closure, which is what R2181 did to R2180's, and
found the walk does not have the property its own documentation claims.

THE HOLE. `next_kind` is an exhaustive match, so a new `FieldValue` variant
does not compile until it is given a SUCCESSOR. Its doc read that as making
`kind_words` "a walk over the type rather than over a list", and `kind_words`'
doc as "a variant added later joins this at `cargo build`". Both are wrong in
the one direction that costs: the compiler forces a new variant to HAVE a
successor and forces nothing to have it AS one. A variant nothing points at is
a source of the chain and never a destination, so it is left out of the walk in
silence -- and the walk is what `doc_revision` declares the family from.

That is item 555's own defect, one layer beneath the fix for it: a closed set
whose declaration can quietly stop being closed. It shares the seam, so it is
paid in this round rather than filed as a new number.

WHY THE FIX IS NOT A LIST, AND NOT A SOURCE COUNT. Safe stable Rust has no way
to enumerate an enum's variants, so nothing in the library can be asked "is the
walk total". Two derives already on the type can be: `serde::Deserialize`
refuses an unknown variant with a message NAMING every variant it would have
accepted, and that list is written by the derive macro off the enum, so it
cannot omit one and it widens at `cargo build`. `Debug`, derived likewise,
names the variant each walked representative is. Both sides of the new gate are
therefore written by a macro and neither by a person -- a hand-written expected
side would have been a third copy of this vocabulary and the second able to go
stale. This is the artifact-derived population rule applied to a question no
capture can answer, the same discipline R2174 used with `cc -dM -E`.

Round 2184.decision_summary:
R2184 closes open-debt item 556: the document contract had no axis for
"which companion keys arrive with which value". `DocumentShape::keys` is a
UNION over the whole document, so it cannot say "sometimes absent" at all;
`ValueFamily` sees the WORD and stops. The sentence a consumer needs -- if
`fields[].kind` is `opaque`, do not look for `value` -- was expressible in
neither, so every consumer read it off whatever the rendering happened to do.
One of them lost `opaque` outright, which is how item 555 was found.

THE SHAPE THE ITEM WARNED AGAINST, AND THE ONE TAKEN INSTEAD. A field on
`ValueFamily` would leave nine of the eleven families carrying an empty
default nothing measures, which is the hole R2181 had just closed on
`planes`. The axis therefore hangs off `DocumentShape` as `carries`, and
`audit` refuses an EMPTY one on the NEWEST revision of any document that
declares families -- every family the library emits today says which of two
things it is, and there is no third state to fall into. An older revision
carries `&[]` because "this revision did not declare the axis" is true of it.

THE CLASSIFIER IS DERIVED, NOT JUDGED, AND IT IS ONE PREDICATE. A family is a
DISCRIMINANT when some key is decided by the word -- one word ALWAYS brings it
and another NEVER does -- and a PASSENGER otherwise. `decides_a_key` computes
that, and both `audit` (over the declaration) and the new derivation gate
(over what the emitters render) call it, so the table and the documents cannot
be judged by two rules.

THE DERIVATION REFUTED THE ITEM TWICE, WHICH IS THE EXPECTED RESULT AND NOT AN
EXCEPTION. Item 556 measured TWO discriminants; there are THREE.
`fields[].offset_space` is the third and no reading of a `match` would have
found it: `packet` is written by the datagram row emitter with a `packet`
index beside it and `stream_byte` by the stream one with `message_at`, so the
word decides the shape through two EMITTERS rather than two arms. And the
item's `encoding_mismatch` companion set named five keys where the render
gives four -- `why` is not among them. Third and fourth prose measurements
refuted on this seam.

WHY A LIST OF SHAPES PER WORD AND NOT ONE SET. Measured: `stream_byte` arrives
in TWO shapes, with `payload_decode` and without, because that plane is
present only when the caller supplied a format map. So the word decides
`message_at` and does not decide `payload_decode`, both at once. An
INTERSECTION would say nothing about `payload_decode` and read as "never" --
the exact confusion `keys` already causes and this axis exists to end -- and a
UNION would say it always comes, which is false. The set of shapes states both
without a third state, and a third state is what an escape hatch is.

WHY THE WALKER IS PER-OCCURRENCE. `companions` is the third object walker,
after `json_keys` and `top_level_entries`, and it reports one entry per
OCCURRENCE rather than a union per word. Measured: a union reports
`fields[].direction == "a"` carrying both `packet` and `message_at`, a shape
no row of that document has, because `a` occurs once in a datagram row and
once in a stream row. Classifying from that is classifying from a set the
document never emitted.

UNMEASURED IS A FAILURE, NOT A PASS. A family observed with fewer than two
distinct words could not have contradicted either verdict, so the gate FAILS
rather than classifying it. Three census families were in that state on the
existing fixtures; `interest_pair_capture` -- two interests, one per
direction, in two modes, over UDP -- supplies the second word for all three,
`offset_space` included, because a datagram link anchors by packet index.

Round 2194.decision_summary:
R2194 WIDENS the feature-gate diagnostic axis from one package to two, and
the second is the one that matters: `wz-runtime-tokio`, the largest public
surface in this workspace and the one an external consumer actually imports.

R2193 closed item 532 by turning "how many features carry this trap" into a
number -- 153 of 521 -- and left the coverage itself as work, at 1 of 153. This
round takes that work. It is not a new debt and closes no item; it is the thing
532's closure was FOR.

WHAT MADE IT AFFORDABLE, and it is the opposite of what the item feared. Item
532 warned that going at this "with probes for everything" would put hundreds
of cargo builds in a lane. Measured here: every probe compiles the crate under
test with `default_closure minus the feature`, and for a NON-DEFAULT feature
that subtraction is a NO-OP. So all 44 probes share ONE feature set, the
dependency is compiled once rather than once per probe, and the cost is 44
throwaway consumer crates rather than 44 builds of a large crate. The item's
fear was about a shape this axis does not have.

THE PROBES ARE DERIVED, NOT TYPED, and that is the round's design choice. A
`#[cfg(feature = "f")]` sitting on a CRATE-ROOT `pub` item means the path
`<crate>::<name>` exists only with `f` on -- which is exactly the sentence a
probe has to falsify, and it is the path a consumer would type, because it is
the one the crate published. Deriving it means a feature added tomorrow gets a
probe without anyone remembering to write one, and a renamed module cannot
leave a probe pointing at nothing. 44 of the package's 62 public-gating
features are answerable this way; the other 18 gate a public item in a
SUBMODULE, where the path needs the module-reachability question R2193
deliberately left open.

SO THE AXIS GAINS A THIRD DECISION STATE. `DEFERRED`: gates a public item, not
probed yet, reason given. It is not an escape hatch, and the reason it is not
is structural rather than promised -- the census reads that table, prints its
size beside the denominator every run, and FAILS on a name in it that no longer
gates a public item. The list can shrink or be corrected; it cannot grow in
silence.

AND THE CENSUS STOPPED BELIEVING THE OTHER TABLE. `NO_PUBLIC_PATH` is a
declaration the diagnostic axis accepts and cannot check, which is exactly the
shape a reason-string table rots into. This round made it a DERIVED claim: a
feature declared to gate no public path, found by the census attached to a
publicly visible item, is now a finding. The 18 declared for this package were
adjudicated that way rather than trusted -- two independent derivations, and
they agree.

⚠ THE DERIVATION COULD NOT FILTER ITSELF, and the first run said so. A crate
root gates DEFAULT features too, and a probe for one of those would turn OFF a
feature a plain build has -- a different question from the one this axis asks.
Six such rows came back as stale before the optional-set filter was added, and
the fix moved the merge inside the per-package loop where the optional set is
known. A derivation that runs before the thing it must be filtered by is not
yet a derivation.

space, and the fault preserves order exactly WITHIN a conduit.

Round 2201.decision_summary:
R2201 closes open-debt item 559, the hosted red R2200 read at its round
start and acked rather than repaid. The subject is `shm_auth_segment`'s
id allocator, and the repair is one shift; what took the round is
establishing that the WITNESS could not be turned green by a scheduler.

The defect. `next_candidate_id()` was
`pid.wrapping_mul(K).wrapping_add(c) | 1`, where `| 1` enforced "never 0"
by flattening the low BIT. Writing `b = pid * K`, that makes
`(b + c) | 1 == (b + c + 1) | 1` whenever `b + c` is even, so every other
pair of CONSECUTIVE counter values collapsed onto one id.

The function's own doc said collisions "are caught by `create_new`
(`O_EXCL`) and retried, so this only needs to spread". That sentence is
true of a collision with a LIVE segment and false of the one that
mattered: retry answers "this id is taken", and an id whose segment was
unlinked a microsecond ago is not taken. Two draws back to back, the
first dropped before the second is created, land on the same
`/dev/shm/<id>.zenoh`, and a reader still holding the first id reads the
second segment's challenge. That is the `Some(42)` Layer C1bn reported.

The repair makes "never 0" STRUCTURAL rather than a correction:
`(b + (c << 1)) | 1`. The shift leaves bit 0 free, so the OR carries no
information away -- every id is odd, hence never 0, and distinct `c` still
give distinct ids. The alternative, special-casing `if v == 0 { 1 }`,
keeps the full 2^32 range but re-introduces exactly one collision pair,
and a rule with an exception is what this function is being repaired FOR.
The trade taken instead: the period is 2^31 draws and every id is odd,
both irrelevant against a retry budget of 100 and a namespace foreign
nodes draw from independently.

The witness is over a PURE `candidate_id(pid, c)`, split out for that
purpose. A test that drew from the atomic would measure whichever values
the other tests in the binary left it -- under `--test-threads > 1` its
draws are not consecutive, and the OLD form separates `c` and `c + 2`
perfectly well. A witness a scheduler can turn green is not a witness.

it understated where the widening had to reach. Both forwarders spend the key at

`node_hlc` is read once per forwarder and nowhere else.

The leg therefore grew a FOURTH proof shape. Each run stands up a three-node star
-- publisher, the node the document configures, subscriber -- and taps BOTH of
that node's links. The outbound tap gives the reading (the Put's `T` flag,
zenoh-protocol put.rs:43, with the `timestamp` at :50 walked as a nested field);
the inbound tap is the control and the anchor, because it says a Put arrived AND
that it arrived bare, so a stamp downstream is this node's and not the
publisher's.

never a pass -- it means the star did not stand up and the run measured nothing
-- while `NoRelay` is a reading about a node that holds two faces and still does
not forward. One word covering both would have let a failed topology read as a
clean partition. `Mixed` is a defect by construction, since zenoh stamps once at
the head. The ARM POPULATION is DERIVED, not listed: relaying needs two faces, and
which run-modes have a listener is `default_listen_endpoint`'s answer -- upstream's
rule that a client never listens is what drops `Client`, and the dropped arms are

THE ITEM'S OWN LAST VERDICT WAS REFUTED, BY ITS OWN LOG. R2203 wrote that this
key was blocked on implementing upstream's RSA exchange, on the strength of
`multilink.rs:44-56` building an `RsaPrivateKey` before the extension is sent.
That is true of upstream and says nothing about wz: the leg's per-arm extension
dump already showed `multi_link` on the InitSyn of the `--max-links 2` arm and of
no other arm. This tree ALREADY offers ext 0x4 above an aggregation budget of one,
because `peer_loop` picks `dial_face_multilink` there (`accept_loop.rs:1786`) and
that establishment negotiates it. What upstream needs the key for is the
challenge's CONTENT; what this list claims is that the frame moved with the file,
and the offer is what moves.

The real obstacle was the COMMAND LINE, which is what R2179 had written before the
RSA sentence was layered on top of it. An argv-typed flag is authoritative over
the file (`args.rs`, `decide_pair`), and two of this leg's arms type
`--max-links`, so no arm could attribute the offer to the DOCUMENT. The fix is
the arm R2179 named as missing — `(PeerMesh, None)` — plus a fifth proof shape
whose only difference from `FIXTURES` is which arms may judge it.

That arm set is DERIVED from `ARMS`'s own second column rather than listed: an
arm that stops typing a number joins the sweep by itself, and an `ARMS` where
every arm types one empties the population and reds.

THE THIRD DOCUMENT IS WHAT MAKES THE SHAPE HONEST. With two, "this arm does not
read the key" and "this arm has the capability on whatever the file says" are the
same pair of equal readings, and the first would have excused the second. So each
kept arm is also asked a document that names the key at all — row A states the
NON-default and row B the default, the baseline must answer what B does on EVERY
arm, and only then is an arm whose two readings both equal that baseline called
inert.

Emptying `not-yet-read` trips that ledger's own per-kind anti-vacuity, which its
comment says is "a decision to record". This round records it. That kind, and only
that kind, may be empty, and the reason is structural rather than written down:
the ledger's population is pinned to `honoured MINUS wire`, so a row leaves by one
route — its key entering the wire list. A mis-sort into `off-wire`, which is what
the comment feared, MOVES a row rather than emptying the kind. The other two kinds
have no route out and keep the old rule.

Round 2206.decision_summary:
R2206 closes open-debt item 561, and the fix is a DELETION rather than a
check. The coordinate space of a decoded message was decided twice: once by
the caller that handed the observer a number, and again by a hand-written
match over the message lists one crate up. The serial line is what that
cost -- it feeds the datagram coordinate path with a capture PACKET INDEX
and the match called it `StreamBytes`, so every plane emitted a packet index
under the word that tells a consumer to add byte spans to it, in exactly the
field that exists to stop a consumer guessing.

The first shape considered was a gate holding the declaration against the
frames. Measuring the consumers refuted it: NOT ONE of them reads the space
of a list with no frames in it -- every one reads it inside `for frame in
frames`. So the space is a property of the FRAME, not of the list, and the
right move was to take it off the enumeration entirely. `decode_framing_unit`
now takes an `Anchor` (a number AND the space it is in) so a producer cannot
hand in the number alone, and there is no second opinion left to keep in
step.

Round 2209.decision_summary:
R2209 closes open-debt item 563. The item asked for a DECISION -- should
`inspect` yield the `NotOnTheWire` verdict, or should this tree record that it
will not -- and re-measuring it moved the question. The per-message marker
already existed: `payload_decode::decode_payload` has returned
`PayloadDecoding::NotOnTheWire` since R2170 and `state()` renders it as
`not_on_the_wire`. What blocked delivery was one condition in the EMITTER --
`fields_json` asked for a decoding only when a caller supplied a payload
mapping, so a consuming surface that declared no format got no block at all.

So `inspect` is untouched and the test asserting its arm stays dead is still
green: that device says "decide when this becomes reachable", and nothing this
round made it reachable.

The decision is to DELIVER, and the argument is not new -- R2170 made it one
level down when it moved the SHM question ahead of the declaration check,
because whether a record's data crossed this wire has nothing to do with what
formats the reader declared. The emitter did not inherit that argument, so the
fact stayed trapped behind the declarations one level up. Every OTHER
`payload_decode` state answers a question about the reader's own declarations
and the old rule is right for those; `not_on_the_wire` is a fact about the
capture, which is why `Verdict::NotOnTheWire` was built as a named absence
rather than left as a silent `no_payload`.

Item 565 was filed as "the Fragment First / Drop markers do not reach the
consumption surface -- the tree measures them and delivers nothing".

true.
THE WIRE FACT WAS ALREADY DELIVERED. `ext_name::FRAGMENT` names `0x2 -> first`

Round 2215.decision_summary:
The budget's second arm, and a verdict on the shape that cannot have one.
THE ARM. `expired_blocker_lint.py`'s `IDENT` was budgeted as a citation and is
not one: it is a regex fragment. The carried brief said it reaches `re` through
an f-string, and re-measured that is wrong -- it reaches it through STRING
CONCATENATION into `ABSENCE_PATTERNS`, which a comprehension then hands to
`re.compile`. Two hops, and the classifier could see neither: it read only the
pattern argument of an `re` call, where the argument is a LOCAL bound by the
comprehension.
So the REGEX arm became a dataflow closure. Three seeds -- an initialiser that
calls `re`, an `re` argument that IS or COMPOSES a table, and an argument
naming a local that iterates over one -- and then a transitive step through
string COMPOSITION only.
THE VERDICT, on the four upstream citations `zenoh-transport`, `WCodec`,
`network/request.rs` and `unicast/establishment/ext/shm.rs`: NO ARM CAN CHECK
THEM, and the reason is measured rather than argued. `git ls-files vendor/`
returns FOUR LINES, because the vendored trees are submodules and their
contents are not this repository's tracked files -- all twelve budgeted tokens
score zero against a vendor corpus that is itself empty. And `.gitmodules` does
not name zenoh at all: sce, zenoh-pico, lwip and freertos-kernel are the four,
so even a checked-out submodule would not resolve these. Making a checkout the
oracle would put a gate on machine-local state, which is what CLAUDE.md forbids
machine-local paths for -- a gate whose answer differs per clone is not a gate.
verification_bullets: THE SELFTEST CAUGHT THE ROUND'S OWN OVER-REACH BEFORE IT SHIPPED. The first
seed read `re.compile(REASONS['k'])` as proof that `REASONS` is a pattern,
which would have exempted an ordinary reason table from ever having its claims
checked -- a FALSE PASS, the one direction a classifier must not fail in. The
narrowness control written beside the widening is what refused it, and the seed
now requires the argument to BE the table or COMPOSE it, never merely to
mention it.
MEASURED BEFORE BUILDING, and it bounded the blast radius: the closure moves
exactly ONE table, `IDENT`, and loses none of the four the old rule caught. The
narrow composition rule (`+`, `%`, f-string, format, join) and a wide "appears
anywhere in the initialiser" rule give the SAME answer over this tree, so the
narrowness costs nothing today and is what keeps the scope from drifting.
TWO MUTATIONS IN THE REAL TREE, one per hop, each reverted: the composition
closure disabled -> `IDENT` falls back to REASON and goes red above budget 0;
the iteration binding disabled -> the same red. Both hops are load-bearing and
neither is decoration.

The third arm, taken the way the carried brief asked: MEASURE WHETHER
DECOMPOSITION IS THE ANSWER BEFORE BUILDING ONE.
It is, and the measurement changed the design twice on the way.
FIRST, word-bounded matching against comment-stripped code resolves six of the

code, because wz DESCRIBES zenoh's `.transmute()` and never performs one. So an
expression citation is a claim about what the documentation says as much as
about what compiles, and the corpus for this arm is whole text.
SECOND, the shape cannot be "has punctuation". With `/` and `-` admitted,
`network/request.rs` decomposes into `network`, `request`, `rs` and
`zenoh-transport` into `zenoh`, `transport` -- every one of which lives here,
so three of item 567's four upstream citations would RESOLVE. Those are the
citations R2215 measured to be uncheckable in this tree, so resolving them is a
false pass wearing the costume of progress.
And the coincidence floor was measured rather than guessed: an expression made
only of one-character identifiers co-occurs in 93 files, so a token carrying no
identifier longer than one character carries no evidence at all. That is not a
tunable threshold -- one is the minimum an identifier can be.

to admit `/` and `-` drops the budget from four to ONE, and the ratchet reports

false pass. Only the SELFTEST tells the truth, naming
`'network/request.rs' was claimed by the expression shape`. A control that
lives in the count could not have caught this; the control has to assert the
arm's SCOPE.

Round 2217.decision_summary:
Item 567 asked one question -- where a "known references list" should live --
and answering it needed a second judgement the item had not anticipated.
JUDGEMENT ONE: THE LIST HAS NO NEW HOME, BECAUSE THE TREE ALREADY HOLDS IT.
Every repository this workspace fetches is already written down twice over in
machine-readable form: the `url` of each submodule, and every `git clone` in a
tracked script or workflow. Derived from those, the set is seven --  `zenoh`,
`zenoh-c`, `zenoh-pico`, `scxml-core-engine`, `lwip`, `FreeRTOS-Kernel`,
`zephyr`. Writing a list would have been the second copy this whole area
exists to prevent.
⚠ The round's FIRST probe answered "zenoh is absent", and it was wrong.
`build-zenohd.sh` writes `git clone --depth 1 --branch "$V" \` and puts the URL
on the continuation line, so a line-at-a-time scan finds the clone and not what
it clones. Joining continuations first is the fix, and it is now a selftest
control rather than a thing to remember.
JUDGEMENT TWO: A DECLARATION MUST NOT BUY A PASS. Written the obvious way --
`zenoh:network/request.rs` RESOLVES -- the budget fell from four to zero, and
that is an escape hatch: the name is checkable against the clone set, and the
part after the colon is checkable by nothing, so `zenoh:` in front of any
invention would have bought silence. So a declaration buys a line in a
different ledger instead. `DECLARED_UPSTREAM` is pinned in both directions
exactly as the budget is, and an author who wants to quiet a citation by
prefixing it still has to move a number and answer for it.
verification_bullets: THE ESCAPE HATCH WAS BUILT AND THEN MEASURED SHUT, in that order, and the
measurement is the evidence. Written as a resolution the arm dropped the budget
from four to zero; rebuilt as a separate pinned ledger, two mutations show it
cannot buy silence.
MUTATION ONE: `zenoh:WCodec` rewritten to `zenohh:WCodec`, a repository this
tree does not clone. BOTH ledgers fire at once -- the declaration count falls
below its pin and the token lands unresolved above its budget -- so a bogus
repository name has nowhere to hide.
MUTATION TWO, the escape-hatch control: a NEW citation `zenoh:whatever-i-
invented` with a legitimate prefix. The declaration pin goes red and names the
token. Prefixing does not silence; it moves a number somebody has to answer
for.
Both reverted. Live: budget 1 citation across 1 file (`west build`), declared
upstream 4 against 7 known repositories, both exactly as pinned. Selftest: 30

  * "the residual statements have rotted" -- those reasons carry 1003 file
    citations; 409 resolve uniquely to a tracked wz path and NOT ONE points

  * "the depth axis has no instrument" -- false for configuration.
    `every_honoured_key_is_classified_by_what_proves_its_effect` already

What IS true is that nothing MEASURED any of that. The numbers were correct and
unwatched, which is the state item 200 describes even though its account of why
was wrong. And the grades had drifted from the register's own record while
nobody looked: PARTIAL is 86, not the 85 the item states.
So the deliverable is the census item 200 itself named as the next instrument,

`audit-catalog-status.sh` already trusts for COMPLETE -- is asked the question
nobody had asked of PARTIAL, and the citations those grades rest on are

round's sharpest verification. It asked whether each PARTIAL reason NAMES a
residual and on its first run flagged `platform-macos` and `platform-windows`.

be FALSE -- and merely spell it in words the axis had not been given. That axis

changes_bullets: THE RULE, pure and in the crate that owns the decision:
`wz_session_core::scout_responder::best_reply_source(asker, candidates)`
-> the index of the address sharing the longest octet prefix. Upstream's
`matching_octets` count, and upstream's tie rule kept deliberately --
`Iterator::max_by` returns the LAST of several equal maxima, so an
identical candidate list in an identical order elects the identical
socket. It takes ADDRESSES, not sockets, which is what makes a
multi-homed election testable on a single-NIC host.
ONE DIVERGENCE, in wz's favour: `leading_equal_octets` returns None
across address families. Upstream's `zip` truncates to the shorter octet
string, so a v4 asker scored against a v6 socket compares four octets of
one against the first four of the other -- a number with no meaning that
can WIN and elect a socket that cannot carry the reply at all.

any whose `local_addr` cannot be read, which is upstream's own filter
(`orchestrator.rs:1130`); `UdpDriver::bind_reply_unicast` binds each on a

partner -- its destination arrives with each datagram, so it is reached
through `send_datagram_to` and never through `LinkDriver::send`.

refused, rather than upstream's `filter_map(.ok())` that silently
shortens the list.

first IPv4 per interface) resolved LIVE per call rather than out of

not determine" where upstream returns the same empty vec it uses for "no
interface qualifies".

single-homed host it is indistinguishable from the elected reply and on a
multi-homed one it is the defect.

carried. 568: the SN-ring and PATCH axes had assertions only over wire this
tree wrote. The register said the resolution key was already honoured -- it is
not, it sits in all three UNHONOURED lists -- and said patch had no handle --
it does, because a stock zenohd answers min(CURRENT, what the InitSyn carried),
so announcing NO_PATCH makes a genuine router genuinely answer 0. The value for
the SN axis lives on the ROUTER (a --cfg on zenohd) precisely because a value
advertised by wz would make the negotiated ring equal wz's own advertisement,
which an implementation ignoring the InitAck also produces. 569: the
wz_dissect_live_* binary door had no witness at all in the interop crate, and
no prose records a decision to keep it out; the sibling witness says of itself
that it asserts existence and never an offset, which is the cell the consuming
surface stands on. Both are graded against the BYTES rather than against a
second decoder, because the two decoders in this tree are one engine and their
agreement proves agreement. The R2199 gate's "somewhere" criterion was widened,
as a separate gate that joins two existing derivations rather than re-deriving
either.

Round 2224.decision_summary:
부채 572 — 협상축 넷(`req_id_res` · compression · lowlatency · qos)이 SYNTHETIC-ONLY.
등록부의 문장을 명령으로 다시 쟀고, **넷 중 둘에서 등록부가 반증됐다**.

⛔⛔⛔ **반증 1 — compression 과 lowlatency 는 «이미» 정품 상대로 증인이 있었다.**
등록부는 「손잡이가 wz 쪽이면 협상값 = 내 광고값이라 InitAck 을 안 읽는 구현도 같은
답을 낸다」고 적었는데, 이 둘은 손잡이가 «라우터»에 있다:
`transport/unicast/compression/enabled`(기본 false) ·
`transport/unicast/lowlatency`(기본 false). compression 은 R311y433 이래
**대조 twin 까지** 갖고 있다(stock zenohd → `negotiated = false`).
그럼 왜 게이트가 SYNTHETIC-ONLY 라 했나 — **접근자를 읽는 자리가 «다른 프로세스»**
이기 때문이다. `wz-ap-demo` 가 `is_compression()` 을 읽어 로그로 내보내고 테스트는
그 «줄»에 단언한다. 게이트는 파일 «안»의 단언만 보니 못 봤다. ⇒ 이건 재정의가 아니라
**거짓 음성의 수리**다.

⛔⛔ **반증 2 — `req_id_res` 는 라우터 손잡이가 «없다».** 등록부는 「`patch` 팔 B 와
같은 지렛대가 통한다」고만 적었는데, 실측하면 상류 config 에 request-id 쪽 키가
아예 없다(`DEFAULT_CONFIG.json5` 의 resolution 키는
`sequence_number_resolution` «하나»고 그건 FrameSN 절반만 움직인다). 라우터 값은
언제나 `Bits::from(RequestId::MAX)` = 2 다. ⇒ 판별 팔은 «내 광고값»을 라우터 값의
«위»(3)와 «아래»(1)에 두는 것이고, 그래야 두 팔이 «다른 값»을 낸다(2 vs 1) —
소비자의 완료조건 ①을 만족하는 유일한 배치다. 위 팔은 wz 가 광고한 적 없는 2 를
읽고(=InitAck 에서만 올 수 있다), 아래 팔은 자기 1 을 지킨다. 둘 중 하나만으로는
「2 를 하드코딩한 구현」과 「자기 광고를 되읊는 구현」 중 하나씩만 배제된다.

▶ **그래서 이 라운드는 «셋»을 한다.**
1. 게이트가 «프로세스 경계»를 넘는 증인을 보게 한다 — 유도로. 코퍼스 파일이
   «모는» 바이너리(`crossimpl_corpus` 의 `cf.binaries`)의 소스에서 그 접근자를 읽는
   `log::` 문을 찾고, 그 포맷 접두사를 테스트의 단언 리터럴과 `shared_head` 로 잇는다.
   ⚠ **넓히는 편집엔 좁힘 대조군** — selftest 팔 넷 중 «셋»이 좁힘이다: 단언 «밖»
   언급은 증인 아님 · 접근자를 «안 읽는» 로그는 증인 아님 · 코퍼스 «밖» 파일은 증인
   아님. 넷째는 「너무 짧아 이을 수 없는 보고」를 **이름 대어 거절**한다(포맷 문자열을
   줄여 게이트를 통과시키는 길을 막는다).
2. `req_id_res` 와 `qos` 에 진짜 팔을 짓는다(둘 다 `wz_negotiated_axes_zenohd_interop`).
   qos 는 값이 «라우터»에 있고(`qos/enabled` true/false), wz 의 광고는 두 팔이 같다.
3. lowlatency 에 없던 **대조 twin** 을 짓는다. 그 레그는 R311y372 이래 `= true` 만
   단언했고 반대쪽이 없었다 — compression 은 갖고 있던 것을 이 축은 못 갖고 있었다.

⚠ **`shared_head` 는 첫 실행에서 «잡음 39건»을 냈다** — 모든 보고 접두사가 공백으로
끝나 공백으로 시작하는 단언 리터럴이 전부 1 자를 기록했다. 고침은 임계값이 아니라
**「낱말이 아닌 겹침은 겹침이 아니다」**(세 글자 이상).

⛔ **게이트 «둘»이 내 작업을 먼저 잡았고 둘 다 상환했다.** ① 헬퍼를
`spawn_zenohd_sn_resolution_and_qos_on_ephemeral_tcp` 로 옮기자
`unhonoured_kind_evidence_gate` 가 red — 그 키의 anchor 가 «정확한 함수 이름»이었다.
고침은 anchor 를 접두사로(트리에 그 접두사를 가진 건 그 계열뿐임을 확인). ②
`audit-crossimpl-proof.sh` 가 링크 수 873 → 877 을 «같은 커밋에서» 요구했다. ⚠ 새
레그 넷 중 «둘»만 링크를 더한다 — 나머지 둘은 대조 twin 이라 `wz-proves: none` 이고,
안 그러면 자기 대조군을 증거로 세는 셈이다.

Round 2233.decision_summary:
Open-debt item 585 CLOSED: the mesh DIAL side now carries every IP-family
scheme, so two wz nodes can meet over a QUIC (or TLS / WS / UDP) mesh face.
The item recorded the gap as "wz cannot dial anything but TCP in mesh mode",
and R2231 had already found the ROOT CAUSE was not a missing transport:
`accept_loop::dial_face` called `TcpStream::connect` directly and bypassed
`session_open::dial_locator`, the scheme dispatcher that has carried
tls / ws / quic / quic-datagram / udp for rounds. This round removes the
bypass and moves the three things that were shaped around it.

The item's own four pieces, taken as ONE edit because R2232 measured that a
half is unrepresentable (adding the field alone breaks `face_drive_loop`'s
destructure with E0027, and wiring nothing to it leaves an unused binding):

(1) ENTRY. `resolve_mesh_dial_target` returns `AnyLocator`, not `SocketAddr`.
    It resolves a DNS name of ANY IP-family scheme (resolution is a property
    of the ADDRESS TOKEN, not of the scheme -- the previous shape resolved
    only `tcp`), and it refuses only what has no address at all.
(2) CURRENCY. `FaceSources::dial_targets: Vec<AnyLocator>`; `dial_face`,
    `dial_face_multilink` and both `_after` twins call `dial_locator`. The
    reconcile channel and the gossip-autoconnect arm move to the same
    currency, because both are mesh dials and both were TCP-only for the
    same reason.
(3) IDENTITY. `desired` / `dialed_targets` / `RedialSchedule` stay keyed by
    the RESOLVED ADDRESS. That is deliberate and is what makes the widening
    safe: before the handshake a target's only name is its address, so two
    spellings of one endpoint must still dedup to one dial. `desired` became
    a MAP address -> dial plan rather than a set, so a re-dial reaches the
    peer over the scheme the operator configured.
(4) TRUST. `FaceSources::dial_config: Arc<DialConfig>`, and the demo's mesh
    run-modes carry `--tls-ca` / `--quic-ca` through a new `DialCertPaths`.
    This is the piece that is NOT a type change, and the reason the
    asymmetry ran deeper than the dial call: the ACCEPT side receives its
    cert once, outside the loop, at bind time; the DIAL side needs it inside
    the loop, per target, at every re-dial. Without it a `quic/` dial lands
    on `dial_locator`'s `cfg.quic == None` typed `Unsupported` -- the
    capability present and unreachable, which is R2203's lesson.

TWO REGISTER SENTENCES WERE REFUTED BY RE-MEASUREMENT, and both mattered.
First, "`Vec<AnyLocator>` because `unreachable!` / a parallel type is not
needed" is only true if something answers for the locators that have no
address. `FaceSources` is public, so a caller CAN hand the loop a
`serial/` target; the loop folds `dial_targets` through the SAME
classification the resolver uses (`mesh_dial_plan`) and REFUSES + REPORTS
what it cannot identify, rather than dropping it silently. Unclassified is
red, not pass. Second, the item's line-number map (destructure at :1674,
construction at :2621, 15 literals) no longer described the tree: measured
here it is 15 `FaceSources {` sites of which :1646 is the destructure and 14
are constructions, across 6 files.

`unixpipe` / `vsock` are still refused as mesh dial targets. That is an
IDENTITY limit, not a transport one, and admitting one means giving that arm

instead of saying "tcp-only". And item 584's verdict (b) -- move the QUIC
leg's far end from zenohd to a wz -- is ENFORCEABLE from this round on,

carry_forward_bullets: THE RULE THIS EARNS, and it is not "check more features". Adding a field to
a `pub` options bundle, or splitting a test, is a change whose blast radius
is defined by a POPULATION nobody in this tree derives by hand: literals
live behind feature combinations, dead code appears only at the SMALL end,
and hand-written counts sit in a lane script. Neither `default` nor
`--all-features` is either end of that axis.
So, for the next round that adds a field to `PeerOpts` / `RouterHatOpts` /
`FaceSources` or a sibling, or that adds/renames a test:
* `bash scripts/lib/nondefault-tests-gate.sh --all-legs` BEFORE the push,
not as a pre-push surprise. It derives its own feature lists.
* the accept-only end too:
`--no-default-features --features routing-accept,transport-link-tcp`.
* `grep -n '_runci_guarded_test' scripts/run-ci.sh` for the module you
touched, and re-run the guard's OWN command. Read `-> N test(s)`.
⛔⛔ AND: DO NOT EDIT THE TREE WHILE A PUSH IS INSIDE ITS HOOKS. The hooks
read scripts and sources from the WORKING TREE, so an edit landing mid-run
can make a gate pass on input the pushed commits do not contain -- a local
green that publishes a red. This round did it (fixing the count guard while
gate 4b ran), noticed, killed the push, and re-ran it against a tree that
agrees with itself. The kill is safe and verifiable: rc=143 and `ls-remote`
unchanged.

Open-debt item 588, filed one round ago, said wz's peer<->peer data plane does
not exist against a stock 1.10.0 peer and that its size had NOT been measured.
It is built here, and the measurement it was waiting for turned out to be three
arms rather than one -- which is the part worth recording, because two of the
three are invisible to any probe that only looks at where the data is sent.

WHAT UPSTREAM ACTUALLY REQUIRES. zenoh's `p2p_peer` HAT never consults a
`Network` at all: declarations walk `tables.faces` and data goes to every face
but the ingress. wz mirrors the `linkstate_peer` HAT instead -- declare and
route along the spanning tree -- and 1.10.0's peer HAT hands `Network::new` a
literal `false` for `full_linkstate` at both call sites (`hat/peer/mod.rs:207`,
`:242`). A graph edge needs BOTH ends to advertise the link (upstream's own
`protocol/network.rs:866-871` gates `update_edge` on exactly that), so against
a 1.10.0 peer wz's tree has no children and every send reached zero faces while
returning `Ok(0)` -- a silent zero that reads as "nobody was interested".

THE THREE ARMS, and why the third is the one that mattered.
  1. ORIGIN DECLARATION -- `flood_to_tree_children`, when the root is self and
     the subsystem is gossip, floods to every direct peer face instead. That is
     the arm the item predicted.
  2. ORIGIN DATA -- `compute_self_publish_forward` asked `directions_toward`
     for a next hop; in gossip there is no transit, so the INTERESTED set IS
     the direction set. Self-filtering, because the caller only uses the list
     to match live faces by zid.
  3. JOIN-TIME RE-ADVERTISE -- and with 1 and 2 in place the probe still showed
     `0 data push(es) received`. A declaration is made ONCE, at startup, and a
     peer that joins later is caught up by the tree-change re-advertise; over
     an edgeless graph `compute_trees` produces an EMPTY delta, so nothing ever
     fired. The demo logs `declared subscriber` BEFORE `face 0 UP`, so the
     declaration was always made to an empty face table. Upstream does this at
     the same point and by name (`repropagate_subscribers` inside
     `new_transport_unicast_face`), and so does this now.

Arms 1 and 2 are what a reading of the send path predicts. Arm 3 is only
visible by RUNNING it, and the round that files a capability gap from a probe
should expect that shape: the send path was one of three things wrong, and the
other two were an ordering and an empty delta.

Round 2237.decision_summary:
R2236's push was refused three times and the third refusal was not about the
push. Gate 4b -- the check that a run-ci count guard still agrees with the
tests a push leaves behind -- reported INPUT ERROR on both guards it reached:
`NO libtest summary in the run's output — this gate measured nothing, so it is
not saying the count is wrong`. The hook then failed the push on it. A gate
saying in its own words that it measured nothing is not a verdict, and this
round is what made it one, because R2236's renames are the first push ever to
reach a LAYER Z guard's test set.

THE CAUSE WAS TWO THINGS, and the first diagnosis was only half of it.

(1) THE ONE UPLIFTED BIN PATH. Cargo uplifts every feature variant of one bin
    to a single path, so `crates/target/debug/wz-ap-demo` is whatever the LAST
    build left. A lane provisions its own demo and then runs its guards; this
    gate runs a guard's command ALONE and inherits whatever the previous
    pre-push step built. MEASURED both ways: with Layer Z's feature set the
    command prints `test result: ok. 6 passed`; rebuilt at bare `cargo build -p
    wz-ap-demo` the same command prints `test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 6
    failed`, six `--peer requires the routing-peer feature` preconditions. The
    gate's summary regex is `^test result: ok\.`, so a FAILED run reads as no
    summary at all -- which is why it reported an input error rather than a
    wrong count.

(2) AND IT WAS ANSWERING ABOUT ANOTHER MACHINE. Provisioning locally did NOT
    fix it, which is what exposed the second half: with `BX` set the gate
    routes the guarded command to a build host, and that host has no demo, no
    `target/zenohd/zenohd` and no `target/zenoh-pico-cli/*`. The measurement
    that settled it is in the routed run's own log: `z_sub binary missing at
    /home/<other-host>/.../target/zenoh-pico-cli/z_sub`.

⇒ A lane that BUILDS A DEMO is a lane whose guards depend on machine-local
provisioning. That is the derivation this fix runs on, and it is why there is
no hand-kept list of "guards that need an oracle": such a list goes stale the
round a lane moves its build line, and nothing would measure that.

Round 2238.decision_summary:
Open-debt item 580 — "wz's TX side has no ABANDON state at all, so there is
nowhere to emit the `0x3 Drop` marker from, let alone anything better than
upstream" — is repaid by BUILDING the state rather than by adding a caller to
the encoder that already existed.

THE DECISION, and what it rejects. The registered item said the repair is not
"emit the marker" but "build a finite-budget streaming TX path and put the
abandon branch on it". This round took that literally, and the measurement
behind it is the item's own: `frame_encode::fragment_body` returned
`Vec<Vec<u8>>` — the WHOLE chain minted before a byte leaves — and every link
writer takes `mpsc::unbounded_channel`, so the state "some fragments went and
the rest cannot" was UNREACHABLE. An encoder call added to that tree would
have been a caller on a branch that never runs; the branch had to be made
reachable first.

WHY A SESSION-WIDE BUDGET AND NOT A PER-CHAIN ALLOWANCE. A per-chain
allowance is knowable before the walk starts, and the honest implementation
of it is a pre-check that refuses the whole message and emits nothing — which
never reaches the mid-chain state at all, and so cannot host the abandon
branch. Shared across the session, the credit another sender takes between
two fragments of this chain is not predictable from inside the chain, so the
walk MUST stream and find out. That is the same reason upstream's own
fragmenter streams against its batch pool (`common/pipeline.rs`,
`zgetbatch_rets!`) rather than pre-checking it.

WHERE THIS IS BETTER THAN UPSTREAM, AND WHY THAT IS THE POINT. Item 575
measured that NO implementation puts `0x3 Drop` on the wire at the 1.10.0
pin: zenoh (Rust) reaches its emit site and the encode fails against a reader
`fragbuf.clear()` has just emptied, so the codec rewinds the header away and
an EMPTY batch goes out; zenoh-pico's one call site passes `false`. Every
RECEIVER honours the marker — zenoh at
`io/zenoh-transport/src/unicast/universal/rx.rs:180-185`, pico at
`vendor/zenoh-pico/src/protocol/codec/transport.c:442`. The north star is the
replacement of zenoh and zenoh-pico; a sender-side defect that all of them
share is exactly the kind of gap wz should close rather than reproduce, and
closing it costs no drop-in compatibility because the extension is a
zero-payload unit both receivers already read.

THE SN, which is where wz deliberately diverges. Upstream stamps its stop
fragment with the next conduit SN and does not spend it — invisible there
only because the batch never reaches the wire. wz SPENDS it, because zenoh's
receive-side `SeqNum::roll` (`common/seq_num.rs:145-155`) accepts a transport
message only when its SN advances the window and rejects a repeat, so a
marker that did not spend its SN would make the NEXT chain's first fragment
unreadable to a real zenohd. That is not a theory: removing the reserve
reddens the cross-impl leg and nothing else.

DEFAULTS. The budget is `usize::MAX` ("unbounded") and is never decremented
there, so a profile that never configures one fragments exactly as before,
byte for byte. The stop fragment is drawn OUTSIDE the budget: it is the
abandon NOTICE, not chain payload, and a budget that could not afford to say
it had run out would leave the peer holding the buffer this whole mechanism
exists to release — the same reason upstream builds its stop batch outside
its pool.
verification_bullets: MEASURED THIS ROUND, not quoted.

M2 the "nothing emitted yet" arm is disabled, so arm A announces an abandon

M3 the credit draw always succeeds -> the publish returns `Ok(0)` where the
leg requires `Err(FragmentChainAbandoned)`.
M4 the marker does not spend its SN -> the CROSS-IMPL leg reddens and the
other two zenohd legs stay green: "after the 0x3 stop fragment, the NEXT
chain never reached pico within 12s". This is the one that says a real
zenohd took the marker AS A MESSAGE rather than tolerating it.

is worth more than the arm. The cross-impl leg first reused the file's
existing RETRY loop for the post-abandon publish, and under M4 it stayed

z_sub: `running 3 tests` / 3 passed.

⚠ WHAT THIS ROUND MEASURED AND COULD NOT DELIVER, stated rather than hidden.
Item 580's completion condition (3) asked to observe a real zenohd CLEARING
its defragmentation buffer on the marker. That is NOT observable from a
conforming sender, and upstream's own receive path says why
(`unicast/universal/rx.rs:176-185`): `ext_first` clears the buffer too, on
the very next chain. So "abandoned then started a new chain" and "just
started a new chain" leave a downstream peer in the SAME state — same
delivery, same SN window, same empty buffer — and the only difference is WHEN
the buffer was released, which nothing upstream reports. Separating them
would need a fragment CONTINUING the abandoned chain without `0x2`, i.e. wz
deliberately violating the contract its own marker just stated. The leg
therefore witnesses that the marker is EMITTED and ACCEPTED, and treats the
clear as upstream's documented consequence of accepting it. Conditions (1),
(2) and (4) are met as written: (1) the budget is finite and its exhaustion
is driven by COUNTS, never by a deadline; (2) the marker rides only the
mid-chain arm, and M2 is the mutation that proves the other arm stays silent;
(4) both controls are inside the same assertions, one wz<->wz and one against
the router.

Open-debt 592 recorded two things: wz could not negotiate SHM with a zenohd
built at the pin, and the lane that measures it had been GREEN for months

R2228's pin move could not touch. Re-measured this round, the first is right

The item said, in as many words, that the wire types are identical across the
two releases -- `commons/zenoh-protocol/src/transport/init.rs` declares
`pub type Shm = zextzbuf!(0x2, false)` at both -- and concluded "1.10.0 changed
the ext shape" was disproved and should not be chased. That reading looked at
ONE surface. `transport/open.rs` declares the same name, and there it moved:

    open::ext::Shm   1.5.0  zextz64!(0x2, false)
                     1.10.0 zextzbuf!(0x2, false)

Four things moved together, and the first is the one that kills leg 1:

  1. THE CHALLENGE IS NO LONGER INVERTED. 1.5.0 stored `!challenge` in its
     auth segment, with an upstream comment justifying it as anti-probing
     between versioned implementations. 1.10.0 stores it verbatim. The three
     scalar fields kept their byte offsets, so this is invisible to an
     offset-by-offset reading and surfaces only as a peer whose echo never
     validates: zenohd reads byte 8, echoes what it finds, and wz compares it
     against the un-negated value it holds.
  2. THE SEGMENT IS A STRUCT, NOT AN ARRAY. `ArrayInSHM` of four u64s (32
     bytes) became `StructInSHM<AuthSegmentID, ShmTransportMetadata>`, a
     `#[repr(C)]` struct of 12288 bytes: three u64 scalars, `protocols:
     [ProtocolID; 256]` where `ProtocolID` is now a u32, and
     `shm_counters: [AtomicU32; 762 + 2048]`.
  3. SHM_VERSION 1 -> 2.
  4. THE OPEN PHASE CARRIES HANDOFF COUNTERS. OpenSyn is
     `VLE(challenge) ++ HandoffCounterIds` and OpenAck is the counter block
     alone, where `HandoffCounterIds` is a RAW status byte (0 = Disabled,
     1 = per-priority) followed by one VLE per band. Bands are 8, which is
     `Priority::NUM = 1 + Background(7) - Control(0)`.

and a population of zero is a hard fail rather than a green. The version comes
from the BINARY's own `--version`, because mtime, the workflow cache key and
the metadata sidecar are all claims something else made about it.

Round 2241.decision_summary:
Stop citing upstream by line number, and make the replacement a predicate a
command evaluates rather than a convention people remember.

`CLAUDE.md` asks for a `file:line` citation on every source claim. For THIS
tree's sources that is right: we move those lines, and the commit that moves
them fixes the citation in the same breath. Upstream is the opposite case --
we do not move it, it moves without us, and a stale line number does not
become an error. It becomes a SILENTLY DIFFERENT claim, pointing at whatever
now happens to sit on that line. Open-debt 581 recorded 208 such citations and
the owner's decision of 2026-09-01 settled the form: no line numbers for
upstream, anchor on a symbol or a piece of syntax, and make the anchor
RESOLVABLE so a bump produces a red list instead of a quiet lie.

Measured before this gate existed, against the pinned 1.10.0 checkout:
SEVENTEEN citations were wrong that day. Five named a file that does not exist
at the pin, two pointed past the end of the file they cite, and ten more were
bare mentions of a deleted path. Two of the seventeen were written by R2240 --
the round that had just established, in prose, that 1.10.0 split
`establishment/ext/shm.rs` into `ext/shm/{mod,auth,handoff,segment}.rs` and
then cited the file it had just said was gone.

THE ANCHOR FORM IS DECLARED, NOT INFERRED, and that was a measurement rather
than a preference. The first draft treated "a backticked token near a path" as
the anchor and reported 18 of 42 unresolved; reading them showed the tokens
were mostly not anchors at all -- `wz-codecs` (our own crate name), `{ router,
peer, client }` (a paraphrase), `scouting/{multicast,gossip}/autoconnect_strategy`
(a config key). A gate that guesses which backtick is load-bearing produces
findings about text nobody wrote as a citation. The form is

    `<upstream path>` @ `<needle>`

chosen because the tree had ZERO occurrences of `@` in that position, so no
legacy sentence can be mistaken for an anchor. Both halves are checked: the
path must exist at the pin AND the needle must occur in that file, so a
refactor that deletes the symbol kills the citation loudly.

THREE BUCKETS, EVERY OCCURRENCE IN EXACTLY ONE, and anything the scanner
cannot place is a hard fail rather than a skip: ANCHORED, LINE (the old form)
and BARE (a path with neither). BARE is not an exemption -- it and LINE are
ratchets checked in BOTH directions, so a commit that adds one reds and a
commit that removes one must lower the budget with it. That is condition (2)'s
"gradual, never a bulk rewrite, but locked".

⛔ AND IT REFUSES RATHER THAN PASSING WHEN IT CANNOT MEASURE (condition 3):
no reachable pinned checkout, a population of zero, or an ANCHORED population
of zero -- the last because the needle-resolving half would otherwise be a
branch nothing ever takes. That arm was genuinely empty until this round
populated it by repairing the seventeen.

A gate that DEFERS half of itself has to prove the deferral arrives
somewhere, and the CI that runs it has to carry the tree it resolves

R2241 shipped the upstream-citation gate single-armed in Layer C0, and it
red on EVERY hosted run under its own condition (3) -- "a gate that cannot
measure must not report green". The cause was not the rule but the
placement: measured on the two hosted C0 jobs (`ci`, `validate-codegen`),
neither provisions a zenoh source at all -- zero mentions of
`build-zenohd`, `ZENOHD_SRC`, `zenoh-src` or a cargo checkout between them
-- so "no pinned checkout is reachable" is a fact about the runner, not
about the tree. Re-measured this round: scanning this tree against the pin
and against an empty directory yields IDENTICAL bucket counts and budgets,
and 6 findings versus 385. The classification needs no upstream source;
every finding needs one. That is the seam, and it is where the gate splits.

SO THE GATE HAS TWO ARMS. Layer C0 grades the FORM (buckets, both
ratchets) and can always measure. Layer Z runs `--check --resolve`, because
Layer Z is the lane that builds zenohd and therefore has a source tree, and
there "no checkout" is a real failure rather than a fact about the runner.
`upstream_feature_census.py` already splits on exactly this line, and like
it, the form arm PRINTS its deferral so a green form run cannot be read as
"every citation resolves".

⛔ THE SPLIT OPENED AN ESCAPE HATCH ONE LEVEL UP, AND THE SAME ROUND BOLTS
IT. `--resolve` is a flag someone can simply stop passing: delete the Layer
Z line and the form arm goes on printing "DEFERRED to Layer Z" while
nothing resolves anything and every lane stays green -- condition (3)
defeated by the very split that exists to honour it. So the arm that DEFERS
is the arm that must show the deferral arrives: the form arm now FAILS
unless a live, NON-COMMENT line of `scripts/run-ci.sh` invokes this gate
with `--check --resolve`. Comment lines are excluded deliberately, and it
is a live case rather than a hypothetical -- Layer C0's own comment block
discusses resolving at length without invoking it, so counting prose would
make the check satisfiable by the sentence that describes the problem.
Measured on this tree: ONE live invocation (`scripts/run-ci.sh:12768`),
ZERO comment-only mentions.

THE CHECK LIVES IN THE GATE, NOT IN A SECOND LINT, for the reason
`upstream_root()` reuses `upstream_anchors()` instead of discovering the
pin again: two derivations of "is the resolution arm wired" can disagree,
and that disagreement is what open debt 578 was opened for.

shallow clone `build-zenohd.sh` makes, and only `target/zenohd` was cached

cannot, because a citation added by a LATER commit has to resolve without

installed" the same observation. They are cached TOGETHER rather than under
a second key, so the tree that resolves the citations is the same tree that
built the oracle the interop runs against -- two entries could drift, which
is the two-identities trap R2109 named here first.

gains a `-src` token, and the assert is two DIFFERENT probes -- the
directory can exist as an empty restore, so the second reads the protocol
crate's own lib root, which `upstream_root()` requires of any candidate

EIGHT RED JOBS WERE FIVE CAUSES, AND FIVE OF THE EIGHT WERE TWO LINES.
That is the finding this round starts from, and it was measured from the
job logs of run 33468082489 (`0f2cbbbc`, run_attempt 1) rather than

The two lines:

    clippy::identity_op   wz-session-core/src/extshm.rs
                          `SHM_PRIORITY_BANDS: usize = 1 + 7 - 0`
                          reds Layer C1af AND Layer C1bf
    clippy::for_kv_map    wz-runtime-tokio/src/linkstate_forward.rs
                          `for (_id, state) in self.faces.borrow().iter()`
                          reds Layer M, Layer C1bl AND Layer C1y

⛔ NEITHER IS REPAIRED WITH AN `#[allow]`, AND NEITHER IS REPAIRED THE WAY
CLIPPY SUGGESTED. Both lints were pointing at something real.

`SHM_PRIORITY_BANDS` is a SECOND DERIVATION of a fact this crate already
owns. `qos::Priority::NUM` is three modules over, unconditional, and is
what the conduit arrays (`session_actions.rs`), the Join QoS reader and
the dissect band table already size themselves from. The constant's own
doc argued about how to spell 8 -- "DERIVED rather than copied" -- while
`qos.rs` simply writes `8`, so the tree held two spellings of one number
and a band count that drifted here would have disagreed with the conduit
array silently. The repair is the alias, and clippy's suggestion (`1 + 7`)
would have kept the duplicate while silencing the lint. The unit test that
pins `SHM_PRIORITY_BANDS == 8` stays, and gains its reason: it is now the
one place where the alias is checked against upstream's own number, and
`Priority::NUM` drifting would resize a counter block on the wire.

`gossip_neighbour_zids` destructures a key it discards. The face id is not
part of that walk's question -- a neighbour is named by the zid its
handshake carried, and `fan_out` matches on that -- so `values()` is not
a shorter spelling, it is the accurate one. `fan_out_qos`, twenty-two
hundred lines up, keeps `iter()` because it genuinely uses the id.

⛔⛔ BUT THE ROUND'S SUBJECT IS THE GATE, NOT THE TWO LINES. Five red jobs
from two lints is not two typos; it is a class with no local instrument,
and this tree's own threshold for building one is "leaked more than
twice".

WHERE THE HOLE WAS, measured rather than argued: `pre-push` runs no clippy
at all -- the hook says so in three separate comments and lists clippy
under "STILL NOT covered locally". Gate 3 is `cargo test -p <pkg>` at
DEFAULT features, and both lines sit in code only a non-default feature
compiles, so the crate that MOVED was tested green while the failure
surfaced five jobs away. Every lane that lints such code (C1bf, C1af, C1y,
C1bl, M) is hosted.

THE REPAIR IS A VERB, NOT A NEW GATE. `nondefault-features-gate.sh`
already ran over exactly the right population -- the changed crates that
have a non-default feature, derived from cargo metadata -- and already
used `--all-features --all-targets`. It just ran `cargo check`. R2133
chose that deliberately and wrote the reason in the file: "this class is a
hard compile error in code rustc never saw, and check is the cheapest
thing that hands the code to the compiler". The first half is still true;
the second under-served the blind spot, and this round is the measurement
that says so. The blind spot was never "rustc has not seen this code" --
it is "nothing local has JUDGED this code", and hosted judges it with
`-D warnings`.

So gate 7 and Layer C1cn now run `cargo clippy … -- -D warnings`, spelled
exactly as Layer C1bf spells it, because two spellings of one lint
configuration disagree the day either moves. clippy is rustc plus lints,
so R2133's compile-error class is unchanged at the same targets. Nothing
about the population or the tier lists moved. The diagnostic is now SHOWN
rather than sent to /dev/null: a compile error's text is reproduced by
re-running the command, but a lint's text IS the finding.

⚠ NO TIER ROW WAS ADDED, AND THAT WAS THE THING TO CHECK. Widening a
gate's verb can red crates the push never touched, and the honest
sequence is to measure before deciding whether an exemption table is
needed. The full sweep over all 19 members came back CLEAN with the two

C1bl, M and the transport-link family each clippy a specific feature
subset; `--all-features` covers those features as a superset but is not
the same build, so a lint that only fires when feature A is on and B is
off is still invisible here. That is open-debt item 374's axis and it
still has no instrument. What closed is narrower and exact: every line of
a changed crate's non-default code is now JUDGED by something local, at
the same lint level hosted uses.

THE FAILING ARM WAS THE ORACLE, NOT WZ — AND THE HONEST REPAIR IS
NEITHER TO SKIP IT NOR TO PATCH UPSTREAM'S SOURCE, BUT TO PIN WHAT
UPSTREAM CANNOT DO IN A FORM THAT REDS WHEN IT CAN.

Layer C1ce leg 5 panicked with `the reference z_get_shm exited None`. The
first move was to establish WHOSE failure that is, because the message
does not say: `None` is death by signal, and the arm that died is the one
linked against the genuine `libzenohc.so`.

⛔ WHAT IT IS NOT, each ruled out by measurement rather than argument:

  * NOT a hosted-runner environment problem. Reproduced locally, byte for
    byte, on a machine with a 16 GB `/dev/shm`.
  * NOT a stale or mis-versioned oracle. The hosted job rebuilt it (cache
    MISS on `zenoh-c-shm-1.10.0-…`), and the local one reports
    `Version: 1.10.0`. The examples clone is at the same 1.10.0 tag.
  * NOT the oracle being broken in general. FOUR sibling legs in the same
    file drive that same installation green in the same lane run.
  * NOT wz. Same C source, same argv, same real zenoh-pico queryable: the
    wz arm exits 0 and prints the reply.

WHAT IT IS, derived from source. `examples/z_get_shm.c` sizes its
provider at exactly `strlen(payload)` and then asks that same provider
for exactly `strlen(payload)` bytes. Upstream's own convention one file
over is the opposite: `z_pub_shm.c` takes a 4096-byte provider and
allocates `total_size / 4` from it. The refusal comes from
`commons/zenoh-shm/src/api/protocol_implementations/posix/posix_shm_provider_backend_talc.rs`
@ `Error initializing Talc backend!` -- `talc.claim` over a span too
small for its own bookkeeping. And the crash rather than a clean exit is
a second defect in the same six lines: `z_get_shm.c` does not check the
result, while `z_shm_provider_default_new` returns `Z_EINVAL` on failure
and leaves its out-parameter UNINITIALISED, so the next `z_loan` reads
uninitialised memory. Every other call in that file gets an `exit(-1)`.

MEASURED ON THE SIZE AXIS rather than asserted, every size argv can
carry: 1 / 15 / 18 (the example's own shipped default) / 1024 abort in
Talc init; 2048 / 4096 / 8192 / 16384 / 32768 / 65536 / 100000 / 131071
get past Talc and fail the allocation. THERE IS NO SERVICEABLE SIZE, so
"pass a bigger payload" is not a repair. And upstream CI only BUILDS its
examples -- `cmake --build . --target examples`, never a run -- which is
how a program in this state ships.

⚠ THE FIRST VERSION OF THAT TABLE WAS WRONG, and it is recorded because
the error is the one this project keeps meeting: it reported 1 MiB as
"reached the wire", and that row had never executed at all --
`argument list too long`. A negative result and a probe that could not
fire look identical unless something separates them BY NAME, so the
probe now classifies a dead row explicitly.

A SIXTH CAUSE, AND IT WAS HIDING BEHIND THE THIRD. R2243 read the eight
hosted reds as five causes and put Layer M under the `for_kv_map` clippy
line, on the evidence the log gave: at `0f2cbbbc` that lane died with
`could not compile wz-runtime-tokio`. That attribution was RIGHT ABOUT
WHAT KILLED IT AND WRONG ABOUT WHETHER IT WAS ALONE. With the compile
error gone, Layer M went red again at `b2dd9139` on a different leg
entirely — which is this tree's own recorded lesson (R2235: "a lane's
first red is not that lane's population") arriving a second time, and the
reason a re-measurement refuting the ledger is the expected value rather
than the exception.

THE LEG:
`wz_scout_discovers_zenohd_over_multicast_and_opens_the_advertised_locator`.
wz emits a multicast Scout, zenohd answers with a Hello, and wz is
supposed to dial the locator that Hello carries. It reported
`--scout found no peer on 224.0.0.224:7446 within 10000ms`.

⛔ AND THE CAUSE IS NOT THAT THE HELLO WAS LOST. The demo's own counters
say the Hellos arrived and were recorded — `record_hello` tracks the
FSM's `record_hello_and_emit` dispatches and it climbed with every scout.
What arrived named nothing to dial.

THE MECHANISM, read from the pinned source rather than inherited from
prose: `zenoh/src/net/runtime/orchestrator.rs` @ `fn get_hello_locators`
returns `get_locators()` when the asking peer's IP is loopback and
`get_locators_noloopback()` for everyone else. A multicast Scout never
arrives from loopback. So a router told to listen on `tcp/127.0.0.1:0`
has every one of its locators filtered out of its own reply, and answers
a Hello with an EMPTY list.

MEASURED ON THIS TREE, one variable and two arms, the same zenohd binary
and the same demo:

    listen=tcp/127.0.0.1:0  ->  0 `scouted peer locator` lines, `found
                                no peer`, 288694 Scouts emitted
    listen=tcp/0.0.0.0:0    ->  1 such line, `session Established`, and
                                the Hello carries the host's real
                                interface locators

⚠ THE FIRST VERSION OF THAT PROBE WAS DEAD AND SAID SO, which is the only
reason the mistake was visible: it waited on `Joined multicast group`, a
line zenohd prints only at DEBUG, while running the router at its default
level. Both arms reported `PROBE DEAD`. The env and both needles are now
copied from `spawn_zenohd_multicast_scouting_listening_on` rather than
guessed.

⛔⛔ R2230 ALREADY FOUND THIS CLASS AND RECORDED ITS POPULATION AS ONE.
Its doc on `spawn_zenohd_multicast_scouting_on_any_interface` says the
any-interface listener exists "for the one caller that needs the Hello to
carry a locator". There were TWO, and the second is this leg. The
population is DERIVABLE rather than remembered, and the derivation is
direction, not counting: of the three callers of the loopback form, the
other two (`zenohd_scouts_wz_interop`,
`zenohd_scouts_wz_router_interop`) run the OPPOSITE direction — zenohd
asks, wz answers — so zenohd's own locators never reach an assertion
there. Only a test that dials what the Hello advertised is affected.

THE REPAIR IS THE ADDRESS, NOT THE ASSERTION. A separate
`_on_any_interface_with_args` entry point, for the reason the file's own
`spawn_zenohd_multicast_scouting_with_args` gives one screen up: a new
entry point rather than a changed signature keeps the existing call sites
byte-identical.

TWO ASSERTIONS HAD TO MOVE WITH IT, AND BOTH GOT STRONGER RATHER THAN
WEAKER:

  * the locator check pinned the literal `tcp/127.0.0.1:{port}`. Its own
    comment says what made it sharp: "the port was chosen by the kernel
    and never passed to the demo". Under `0.0.0.0` zenohd announces that
    same port on each real interface, so the PORT is pinned and the
    address literal — which was never the claim — is dropped. Pinning
    `tcp/0.0.0.0:` instead would be worse than useless: that literal
    never appears in a Hello, which expands to the interfaces.
  * a NEW assertion refuses a loopback locator outright, because the port
    check alone would pass again the day `get_hello_locators` starts
    answering `127.0.0.1` — and that is precisely the state this leg
    could not dial from, so it must not read as a pass.
  * the session check compared against the same literal. It now reads the
    locator BACK OUT of the scouted line, which is the stronger claim: it
    binds what wz dialled to what the Hello said, instead of to a string
    the test already believed.

right one, so the repair was the PROSE. What had no instrument at all

reader looking for it, or is read as evidence a hole is handled, which

(`scripts/**`, `.githooks/**`, `.github/**`): 168 names spelled as code,

sentence itself says does not exist -- an example of a typo'd catalog

belongs to a dynamic loader, DT_SONAME to the ELF format,

files whose prose names it, and `foreign` must name an owner that is

any capitalised token inside any backtick gives 13 unresolved, five of

fallback that was removed, and quoting something absent is not claiming
it exists. A span whose whole content is ONE identifier asserts
existence; a span holding a command or an expression does not. Sigils
and the `=value` of an arming stay in (`$SCE_WORKSPACE_ROOT` names a

Round 2254.decision_summary:
ONE SET COULD NOT ANSWER TWO QUESTIONS. R2247's LIVE axis put readers
and setters in one `live` set, so it could ask whether a flag exists
somewhere and nothing else. The two questions that matter are separate
and fail for opposite reasons: a workflow that ARMS a handle nothing
reads pays for a promise nobody keeps, and code that READS a handle no
lane arms has a branch no job can take. `surface()` now returns `(named,
read, armed, where)` and each difference is RED, with the floor on each
minuend because a set difference from an empty set agrees with anything.

THE ITEM'S PREMISES SURVIVED RE-MEASUREMENT, WHICH IS RARE HERE.
Armed-and-never-read is 0, exactly as filed. Read-and-never-armed is
exactly one, WZ_PORT_RACE_REQUIRE, exactly as filed. The item's warning
that a naive set difference gives four did NOT reproduce, and the reason
is worth keeping: `armed` already counted a lane script's `FLAG=1 cargo`
prefix as well as a workflow's `env:` key, so the three flags that
warning was about were never in the difference. That warning was
conditional on looking at workflow env alone.

THE PRESCRIPTION DIVERGED, AND THE MEASUREMENT IS WHY. The item said to
close the live defect by arming the flag. It cannot be armed, and not
for want of wiring. Its precondition is whether the kernel re-hands a
just-released ephemeral port, which is neither a file nor a program, so
it falls outside the closed pair of oracle kinds `armed_oracle_census.py`
can probe -- a closure whose own reason is that a kind no shell one-liner
can decide is a row nobody can check remotely. And a lane that
established the property first would be arming on the result of the very
draw the test then judges, which cannot disagree with itself. Arming is
vacuous BY CONSTRUCTION. So the branch and the flag are gone and the
test's doc comment records why, which is the durable half. Measured while
deciding: this host DOES provoke the race, 10 repeats in 256 draws -- so
the reason is not "no host can", it is "no place can arm it".

FIXING THE AXIS FOUND A MEASUREMENT DEFECT IN IT. The setter regex was
`\bFLAG\s*[:=]`, and `${FLAG:-0}` puts a `:` immediately after the name.
Every shell READ was therefore counted as an ARMING, which means the
read-and-never-armed axis could never have fired in shell at all -- the
new rule would have shipped able to find only the Rust instance. A
lookbehind separates an expansion from a workflow's `FLAG: 1` key and a
lane's `FLAG=1` prefix.

AND THE NEW AXES RAN NOWHERE UNTIL THEY WERE MADE TO. `surface()` was
`root is None` only, so no fixture could drive it and the three
set-difference rules were graded by nothing. It takes a root now, and
every fixture gets a base that arms the flag the fixtures read plus one
correct shell scope -- without which all four existing fixtures go red on
the new axes instead of on their own subject. That is the third round
running in which extending a gate turned its own fixtures red first, and
each time the fixture had to grow to carry the shape.
