Round 2447.decision_summary:
Open-debt item 696, PRIORITY head and the owner's top pick, and the SECOND claim of the ZA-1039 consumer report: a datagram flow row could not say which link it was read off. The reader knew — `DatagramLink::RawEth` is chosen in the first pass, whose own comment calls that site the last place that knows — and then dropped the answer one call later, so the only thing a renderer could ask about a flow was the SHAPE of its address bytes. A raweth endpoint is a 6-byte MAC, `Endpoint::is_ipv4` answers false for it, and the "not four, therefore IPv6" branch printed pico's `30:03:c8:37:25:a1` as `"addr":"3003:c837:25a1","port":0`. The consumer asked for the key and asked, in its own words, that it NOT be inferred from the endpoint shape.

THE PREMISE WAS RE-MEASURED FIRST and stands in full: all of the item's code claims are exact. `DatagramLink` is private, reaches only the handshake question, and `DatagramDissection` has no link-kind field.

THE FACT NOW TRAVELS ON THE KEY, AND THAT IS THIS ROUND'S DESIGN DECISION. `link::LinkKind{RawEth,Serial,Tcp,Udp,Vsock}` is a private field on `FlowKey`, written by the strip that BUILT the key — there is exactly one constructor per kind — and read through `FlowKey::link()`.

WHY THE KEY AND NOT THE DISSECTION, which is what the item's own done-when (1) suggested. Eight emitters in two crates render a flow, and the planes behind FOUR of them — interests, exchanges, and the routing graph's nodes and links — hold a key and nothing else about the flow it came from. A field on `FlowDissection` / `DatagramDissection` would have reached the two row emitters that already have one and left the other six to keep inferring. Done-when (1) is met through `DatagramDissection.flow.link()`: the kind lives to the dissection, and a SECOND field beside it would be one fact in two homes — the argument `FlowKey::serial_line` already makes about the interface count it removed.

THE POPULATION FOR THE SPELLING HALF WAS DERIVED AND IS WIDER THAN THE ITEM'S LIST. Four sites in `wz-capture` spell an address (`census_json::push_endpoint`, `report::flow_text`, `report::push_carrier_line`, and the hop chain in `report::push_carrier_object`) plus one in `wz-analyze` (`endpoint`), and every one of them asked `is_ipv4()` and treated the rest as IPv6. They now share ONE spelling, `Endpoint::addr_text(LinkKind)`. The hop chain is the site that must NOT take it: a carrier hop is an outer IP address read out of an IP header, it belongs to no flow and has no link kind to ask about, so it takes `Endpoint::ip_text()` instead. That is a separation by subject, not a filter.

WHICH SURFACES EMIT IT, NAMED RATHER THAN LEFT SILENT (done-when (2)): the census document at revision 8 and the field document at revision 7, on EVERY flow object of every plane; the summary's tunnel flows, which share the same emitter; `wz-analyze`'s `--flows` framing column, which already mixes framings with link kinds and carries `serial` on exactly that argument; and that CLI's endpoint column. `vsock`'s address spelling is deliberately NOT changed and is filed as item 698.

Open-debt item 695, piece 2 of the hosted red streak: Layer C1bn. The
symptom was one test, `dissect::tests::

emits not matching its pin.

THE VERDICT IS THAT NEITHER DIRECTION HAPPENED. `encode_join` did not
gain and did not lose an extension. The pin and the producer arrived in
ONE commit (`67900182`, R2417) and the pin was written in one build's
terms: relative to it the lane's build emits one FEWER, and the missing
one is id `0x07`, the JOIN protocol-PATCH extension
(`extpatch::PATCH_EXT_ID | ext_header::EXT_ENC_Z64`).

MEASURED, same commit `2941cdd8`, same test, two builds:
`dissect,session-multicast,codec-join,transport-qos` FAILS
`left: [1] right: [1, 7]`; that set plus `transport-fragmentation`
passes. So the set is a FUNCTION of the build and the pin was a single
literal.

THE PIN IS THE DEFECT AND THE EMITTER IS CORRECT. `encode_join`
announces this node's protocol level only where it can emit the
chain-boundary markers the level promises, and that capability is still
`transport-fragmentation`: `frame_encode::multicast_frame_or_fragments`
re-frames an oversize frame under that cfg alone
(`crates/wz-session-core/src/frame_encode.rs:1071`) and returns the
frame whole without it. R2448 widened `build_fragment_wire` -- spelling
ONE fragment message is a codec act -- and deliberately did not widen
the decision to CHAIN, which is transport policy. So the capability the
announcement promises is unchanged, and announcing a level whose markers
this build cannot emit stays worse than silence: a patch-1 receiver
refuses a chain whose start marker never arrives.

R2417 KNEW THE CONDITION AND APPLIED IT EVERYWHERE BUT HERE. Its
sibling `multicast_join::tests::
a_beacon_announces_this_nodes_patch_level` carries
`#[cfg(all(transport-fragmentation, reassembly))]`
(`crates/wz-session-core/src/multicast_join.rs:509`). The one place the
condition is missing is the pin, whose own `#[cfg]` names only the three
features the opaque-row LINKAGE needs.

RE-PINNING THE LITERAL AS `[0x01]` WAS REFUSED AS THE SAME DEFECT
MIRRORED -- right in this lane, wrong in every build that chains. The
expected set is DERIVED from the capability instead, and derived by
asking the emitter rather than by spelling the feature name a second
time: hand `multicast_frame_or_fragments` a frame past the MTU and count
the datagrams. A second spelling of the cfg would be a tautology against
the producer; the derivation instead holds the announcement and the
capability AGAINST each other, so a build that announces a level it
cannot chain, or chains without announcing, reds.

WHY NO LOCAL GATE EVER CONTRADICTED IT. pre-push gate 2h's
`wz-session-core` leg names 95 features INCLUDING
`transport-fragmentation` and runs the whole crate, so it built the arm
where the pin was right and stayed green; hosted Layer C1bn's
multicast-union arm selects the arm without it. The same test held
opposite verdicts in two gates for every completed run since R2417 and
nobody put the two side by side.

two precedents use. The attribute is load-bearing and is a FOOTPRINT
decision, not a style one: out-of-line, the inlining decision cannot
FLIP between the baseline and the minus build, so the name the
catalog's claim is checked by exists in one and not the other. The doc
records the measurement, the two-commit window the red arrived in, and
why the two siblings in the same module were unaffected.
NO intra-doc link was added — every reference is in backticks — so the
Layer C1bz / pre-push gate 4 doc-link budget is untouched by

the map stays the single source, it checks three things: the named
function EXISTS in the named crate; its module half is real (the last
segment is the file's stem or a `mod` that file declares); and it
carries `#[inline(never)]`. Every resolution failure is a FAIL, never a
skip, and an EMPTY POPULATION is a FAIL — a derived subject set that
reports green by finding nothing to grade is the shape this tree has
paid for repeatedly. The count of witnesses read is PRINTED, so
"passed" cannot be confused with "looked at nothing".

shape, because an attribute may span lines (`#[cfg(all(` .. `))]`) and
a shape test for that is a guess. A blank line or comment does not
break the attribute run — Rust attaches across both — but the first
line of real code does, so a boundary belonging to the PREVIOUS item
can never be read as this one's. Both are selftest cases.

Open-debt item 695 piece 3 — hosted Layer F. `measure-codec-footprint.sh`
judges each codec-X atomic feature twice: a BYTE DELTA between the baseline
and a minus-codec-X binary, and a BY-NAME WITNESS
(`CODEC_ELISION_WITNESS[codec-X]`) which must be present in the baseline
and absent from the minus build. The by-name half exists BECAUSE the byte
half is unreliable — a difference of two 2.7MB binaries tracks the CALLER's
inline boundary at that magnitude, which is why three separate rounds
re-pinned a floor (R311y437, R311y580, R311y822).

THE WITNESS HALF THEN INHERITED THE WEAKNESS IT WAS BUILT TO ESCAPE.
Whether a NAME EXISTS in the baseline is itself an inlining decision.
R311y822 pinned codec-close on `encode_close` and recorded the per-symbol
diff `-86 wz_session_core::handshake_encode::encode_close (86 -> 0)`, so
the function was out-of-line THAT DAY and nothing held it there.

The judgement: this is neither a gain nor a loss of elision, and both
obvious repairs are wrong. Re-pinning the witness onto another symbol
repeats the defect one name over. Lowering or deleting the lane discards
the only place codec-close's truthfulness is still judged, since its byte
floor was already retired to -1024 for this same reason. What was missing
is that the property "this symbol is in the baseline" was never made a
property of the SOURCE. `#[inline(never)]` makes it one, and this tree had
already ratified that exact move twice — R311y878 on `decode_keep_alive`
and R311y802 on `declare_envelope_extensions`, the second of which was
itself bisected to a codec-close Layer F red.

The residue shares the seam, so it is paid in the same round: nothing
required a pinned witness to carry the boundary. codec-keep-alive held one
because R311y878 supplied it in the same commit that pinned the witness;
codec-close did not, and the difference was invisible at the point where a
witness is WRITTEN DOWN. `scripts/lib/witness_boundary_gate.py` is that
missing instrument, and it runs in pre-push as well as Layer F because
Layer F is hosted-only by policy — which is exactly how this red survived
three days and roughly twenty-five completed runs unread.

Round 2453.decision_summary:
Item 700's claim was that the census PLANE does not cross the live seam: four `census` doors all take a capture container and none takes a `wz_dissect_live *`, so a consumer watching a running link had the records and none of the five planes. Re-measured at the header before starting rather than inherited: 4 census doors, 0 taking a live handle, 7 live doors, none emitting an aggregate. The reporter's own framing was that this is a DOOR and not a feature, and that held up — the live handle already owns a `Dissection` and the census emitter already takes `&Dissection`, so this round CONNECTS what exists rather than building a second aggregator.
The population question the milestone asked to be named: ONE census door, not four. The container family varies selector x limit preset and names all four combinations; over a handle the LIMIT axis is not an argument, because it was chosen at `wz_dissect_live_open` and is a property of the handle. Taking it again would be the same fact in two places, which is the argument this type already makes about its own cursor. What is left is the selector, and an empty selector is the identity, so `open(NONE)+census("")`, `open(LIVE_TAP)+census("")`, `open(NONE)+census(expr)` and `open(LIVE_TAP)+census(expr)` reach all four.
A SECOND door was forced by the acceptance rather than chosen. The reporter derived the acceptance — the same bytes fed as a container in one go and fed incrementally through the live handle must produce the SAME census — because "a plane arrived" passes over an empty document and this cannot. Probed before designing: on a capture whose last act is an unfilled reassembly gap, those two arms DIFFER, 32 walked records against 94, because the bytes BEHIND a hole decode only once the hole is given up on and `follow` deliberately never spends that patience. A file ends and a tap does not, so a consumer replaying a finite capture through the live doors read a short document with no way to reach the container's answer. `wz_dissect_live_end` is that moment given a name, and it is a separate call from the census because a census must be a READ: spending patience inside a render would mean a dashboard that changes what its own tap decodes.
Both workarounds the reporter had already refused stay refused. Re-feeding a growing prefix to a container door is a new handle each window, so `lost` returns to zero and the census's own cumulative counts cannot be told from a restart; hand-aggregating drained records is a second counter of what this library already counts, and a second counter does not fail, it diverges.

`OpenedSession` hands a caller four working parts and a LIVENESS TOKEN
(`writer_handle`) in one struct with public fields. Rust 2021's disjoint closure
capture takes only the fields a `move` body names, so the ordinary shape

    tokio::spawn(async move { drive_session_until_terminal(
        &mut opened.inbound, &opened.actions, &mut opened.engine, .. ).await })

leaves the token behind to be dropped when the enclosing function returns.
Dropping it SEALS the writer queue (R2367), the socket closes, both sides' drive
loops reach terminal, `release_link` closes the per-link F2 gate, and the first
data send then rejects `TransportUnavailable` — with nothing in the source
reading like a close.

R2423 met this class, repaired the one caller a consumer had reported (wz's REST
bridge against a genuine zenohd), and wrote the trap into `writer_handle`'s own
doc. Prose does not reach the caller written next week: two more call sites had
exactly that shape, and their lanes had been red since R2367.

So the repair is `impl Drop for OpenedSession`, whose only content is the
compiler rule it turns on: a base type that implements `Drop` is captured WHOLE,
because dismantling it would move the `Drop` out from under the value. The trap
stops being reachable from source, at every call site, present and future. Its
cost is deliberate — the struct can no longer be taken apart field by field, so
teardown dismantles through one new `into_parts()` that hands the token back by
name and makes its fate something the caller writes down.

Round 2457.decision_summary:
Open-debt item 702, from a consumer report: the keyexpr id space was
keyed by the FLOW's direction, so a session that aggregated two links
could not resolve its own declarations. Under
`transport/unicast/max_links: 2` a `DeclKexpr` leaves on the link
dialled first and data using the alias may leave on the second; the
declaration and the reference then landed in different table
instances. It never cross-resolved — per-flow is the CONSERVATIVE
BAND around the property "two sessions' id 3 are unrelated", not the
property itself. Exact with one link, too tight with two.

THE UNIT CHOSEN: the session, derived as the unordered pair of node
indices the handshake named. This was checked upstream rather than
assumed — zenoh keeps established unicast transports in
`HashMap<ZenohIdProto, Arc<dyn TransportUnicastTrait>>` and dispatches
an arriving link on `guard.get(&config.zid)`
(zenoh-transport-1.10.0, `src/unicast/manager.rs:108` and `:800`), so
a zid it already holds a transport for means the link JOINS that
transport and only an unknown zid makes a new one. A pair of zids can
therefore hold at most one unicast session, and the pair IS the
session rather than a band around it. The version read is the one
this machine has provisioned in the registry cache — 1.10.0, where
`CLAUDE.md`'s reference paragraph says 1.5.0; the file and lines are
cited so the next reader re-runs the check rather than inheriting it.

THE ORDERING COST, named because the reporter explicitly handed the
weighing over rather than because it was noticed. The node plane runs
over both flow tables and AFTER the decode pass, while keyexpr
interpretation folds as it walks the frames — so a session-keyed
table needs the grouping to exist FIRST. Three ways out were weighed
and two rejected:

* a SECOND PASS — TAKEN. The census walk is the cheap one: the node
  plane matches handshake message kinds and reads no payload, no
  keyexpr and no size, where the throughput plane resolves and sizes
  every record. And `aggregate_grouped` / `interests_grouped` /
  their siblings take the grouping as an argument, so a consumer that
  already computes the census for its own plane hands it in and the
  second walk is not made at all.
* a DEFERRED resolve — buffer the misses and re-resolve once every
  list is folded. REJECTED: it is exactly the retroactive naming the

the two `wz-analyze` lines it reached. The evidence was in hand and thrown away

So this round counted by TYPE rather than by constructor pattern:

truncated — 1 doc comment, 20 tests (16 `payload_decode`, 4 `agg`, both under

R2457 already grouped, 2 from R2458, and 4 left. The four:

  * `field_lines`             -- the human `--fields` stream listing;
  * `datagram_field_rows`     -- its datagram half;
  * `samples`                 -- the REPLAY PLAN's stream half;
  * `collect_datagram_samples`-- the replay plan's datagram half.

THE REPLAY HALF IS THE SHARPER ONE and the register did not name it at all. A
sample's keyexpr is what it will be RE-PUBLISHED under, so an id this walk
cannot resolve does not become a mis-keyed sample — it becomes NO sample,
counted in `Samples::unresolved`. On a `max_links: 2` capture the second link's
publications were simply absent from the plan, behind a floor that read like an

THE SHARED DOOR IS THE INDEX, NOT THE RENDERED SET. `SessionGrouping::owners`
is keyed by the `Dissection::message_lists` position; a renderer keyed on the
two FLOW TABLES cannot compute that position, because a datagram flow
contributes one list PLUS one per QUIC stream PLUS one for its RFC 9221
datagrams. R2458's `RenderedLists` answered it privately inside `fields_json`,
and the register proposed promoting that type. MEASURED and REFUSED: `wz-analyze`
renders the recovered TLS/QUIC rows through `FieldSink` and `fields_json`
cannot, so their rendered-list SETS differ. What is shared is
`node::{stream,datagram}_list_indices` — the index — and which origins a
document renders stays each document's own decision.

They live in `crate::node` rather than on `Dissection`, for two reasons and the
second is process. They answer `SessionGrouping`'s own question inverted —
`owners` maps a list index to a pair of spaces, these map a flow-table row to
its list index — so one module owns the key space both directions. And
`wz-capture/src/lib.rs` carries another session's uncommitted work; committing
it would have shipped half of their pair, since its sibling
`raweth_capture_fixture.rs` would have stayed behind.

AND THE SAME REPAIR CLOSED THE HOLE THAT LET THE WRONG WORD PASS: the

simple cfg at column zero"), which an all-compound feature satisfies

added, with a selftest row (`method_all_compound`) whose reason is stated

second. Under `--no-default-features` the census is one entry shorter,
so the byte-identity oracle red at 296 tracked against 260 emitted,
measured as exactly the `Fragment` packet record, while every
default-feature lane including the pre-push capture gate stayed green.

silently shrunk the shipped sample. The repair splits the two --
`transport_vocabulary` for the artifact, `transport_census` for the MID
censuses -- and rewrites the consumer test to DERIVE its expectation
from `this_build_names` with both arms live and held against each other:
a message the census claims and the reader cannot name reds, and a
message the census disclaims and the reader names anyway also reds,
because then the census is what is stale.

Round 2501.decision_summary:
TWO QUESTIONS THIS ROUND ANSWERED BY READING THE INSTRUMENT RATHER THAN
GUESSING AT IT, and in both the instrument's own text was the evidence.

ONE — CAN `router-connect-reconcile` BE GRADED COMPLETE? NO, AND THE
SWEEP IS WHY. The A3 protocol makes this one binary question ("is there
a nameable residual vs upstream?") and calls COMPLETE the STRONG claim,
to be re-verified adversarially against the WHOLE upstream surface and
never certified from the existing reason. Sweeping upstream's connect
surface -- the connector registry, the dial family, the retry readers
and the close paths -- turned up a capability wz has no counterpart for:
`zenoh/src/net/runtime/orchestrator.rs` @ `pub(crate) async fn terminate_peer_connector(&self, idx: usize) {`
marks one connector settled and fires `notify_one()` when ALL are, and
`start_peer` waits on it with the scouting delay as its timeout.
⭐ THE REGISTRY IS FED FROM THREE PLACES, which is what makes it a
startup-ORDERING guarantee rather than a dial bookkeeping detail: the
dial loop, `zenoh/src/net/protocol/gossip.rs`, and
`zenoh/src/net/routing/hat/peer/interests.rs`. So it means "every peer,
configured AND gossip-discovered, is connected or given up on".
wz has no such thing -- `crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/startup_phase.rs`
is a per-phase RETRY BUDGET with zero occurrences of
notify/barrier/terminated.
⛔ AND THE RESIDUAL WAS NOT FILED AGAINST THIS ATOM, because its owner
is undecided and the protocol says grade PARTIAL when the evidence is
ambiguous -- ambiguous OWNERSHIP is exactly that. It is open item 712,
which also records that two obvious candidates are structurally WRONG
homes: `scouting-active` and `session-unicast-open` are pinned to
zenoh-PICO, and pico has no such registry at all.
⇒ THE LESSON THAT GENERALISES: "every residual is dispositioned" is a
statement about the residual LIST; the grade is a statement about the
upstream SURFACE. Those are different populations, and only the second
one licenses COMPLETE.

TWO — WHAT DOES `Layer U` ASSERT? Its FAIL says a rising number "is open
debt item 579's work, not this table's", and 579 is CLOSED (R2236). So
is the repair a pin bump, or a table move? The module docstring settles

measurement, frozen ... One fewer and it reds too, so that a pin bump
must move this line rather than quietly leaving it high."

handed its remaining condition to 581; 581 closed at R2241/R2242; 579
closed at R2236. Nobody holds "when do we bump". That is the third stale

and the `F=` sentence repeating a withdrawn clause -- and this one lives
